newsitem.title: USA: Sun-Diamond fined $1.5 million in Espy-related case.
newsitem.headline: Sun-Diamond fined $1.5 million in Espy-related case.

text.p: Sun-Diamond Growers of California was fined $1.5 million by a federal court on Tuesday for giving illegal gifts to former Clinton cabinet member Mike Espy.

Sun-Diamond -- the nation's largest fruit cooperative -- also was put on a five year probation, during which the company has to make regular reports to the court to ensure it does not again break federal gratuity laws.

Sun-Diamond was convicted last year in a federal court on eight criminal counts of providing illegal gratuities to former Agriculture Secretary Espy in 1993 and 1994, participating in a scheme to make illegal corporate campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry and violating federal campaign contributions laws.

Acting on behalf of the company, former Sun-Diamond Senior Vice President Richard Douglas allegedly gave Espy expensive gifts and favors, such as a lavish weekend outing at the U.S. Tennis Open Tournament in 1993. Douglas was indicted last year on 19 criminal counts for his dealings with Espy.

Sun-Diamond is owned by five member cooperatives, which are owned by about 4,500 farmers. Sun-Diamond's affiliates, which have not been charged with any criminal wrongdoing, include the nation's largest raisin, prune, walnut, fig and apricot cooperatives.
The affiliates include Sun-Maid Growers of California, Diamond Walnut Growers Inc., Sunsweet Growers Inc., Valley Fig Growers and Hazelnut Growers of Oregon.
Sun-Diamond and its affiliates sell products to the Agriculture and Defense Departments for use in school lunch programs, government commissaries and military cafeterias.
Earlier this year, the government reached compliance agreements with the affiliates, rather than barring them from selling to government agencies.
Sun-Diamond, based in Pleasonton, Calif., has been barred from doing business with the government for three years.

In the sentancing Tuesday, Judge Ricardo Urbino said the company was "willfully ignorant" of the actions of Douglas and that it failed to adequately investigate the allegations concerning Douglas and former Secretary Espy.

Sun-Diamond executives have consistently denied trying to influence Espy with the costly gifts, transportation tickets and favors and have maintained that any favors done for Espy by Douglas were because of a long personal friendship, not an attempt to gain favor with the cabient official.

The Espy investigation, being lead by Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz, has returned indictments or convictions against more than a dozen individuals and concerns, including Espy's former chief of staff and the Washington lobbyist for Tyson Foods.

Sources familiar with the case said the investigation was drawing to a close and that the chief targets of the probe remain not only Mike Espy, but also Don Tyson, senior chairman of the giant Arkansas-based poultry processor and a longtime close friend of President Bill Clinton.
